title: Keep training data as a list of segments instead of concatenating
description: Partitions are stitched by concatenating segment arrays, which creates artificial boundaries between non-contiguous segments (e.g. train blocks before and after a test/anomaly period, or train data from several days). Store each partition as a list of segments and have training iterate over them in a loop.

title: Multi-day nettraffic datasets
description: 8 one-day sets, each with one anomaly. Training data must not contain anomalies but can be stitched from clean segments of many days. Tests should cover several different anomalies, so keep a few days in reserve as test days.

title: Allow choosing the output folder / dataset name in preprocess.py
description: Output always goes to processed/<dataset>; output_folder is not exposed on the CLI. Only names in the datasets list or starting with 'TOL' are accepted, so e.g. 'nettraffic_day1' is skipped even though load_data would dispatch it. Currently worked around by renaming the output folder by hand.

title: Unify TOL --window and nettraffic --interval
description: Both aggregate time into rows, but TOL uses --window (segment lengths in seconds, divisible by the window) while nettraffic uses --interval (segment lengths count intervals). --window is not passed to nettraffic. The --segment help says SECONDS, which is wrong for nettraffic. Defaults differ: CLI --interval is 10, load_nettraffic defaults to interval=1.

title: General preprocessing method / common dataset format
description: Datasets are formatted differently from each other and the nettraffic format has changed. Design a more general preprocessing method instead of per-dataset loaders.

title: Anomalous device can fall outside top-k IPs
description: In the 2026-10-03 test (--top-k 10), 10.78.1.129 got its own columns but 10.78.1.126 (also anomalous, doubletemp) did not, so its temperature is averaged into other_internal_mean_temp. Top-k by packet frequency may drop devices whose signal is in temperature.

title: ipykernel not declared in project dependencies
description: ipykernel was pip-installed into the AaltoAD env so VS Code can use it as a Jupyter kernel, but it is not in requirements.txt or pyproject.toml.

title: load_data reads global args for nettraffic options
description: The nettraffic branch of load_data uses args.port_entropy, args.bytes and args.temperature from the module-level args set in __main__, instead of function parameters. Calling load_data from anywhere else (imports, tests) raises NameError.

title: Fill in authors in pyproject.toml
description: Update authors in pyproject.toml to use local team names and revise later if needed. The authors list is currently empty. Moved from TODO.md, which also had a stray trailing line 'TranAD Contributors' (likely a leftover author entry).

description: Create a CITATIONS file to document references and citations for the project. Moved from TODO.md.
